name: Citizenship by Naturalization

requirements.blocker_text: Law No. 03/L-034 on Citizenship, Article 10: at least 5 years of regular residence under valid permits, having reached the age of majority, elementary knowledge of one of Kosovo's official languages, sufficient material means to support any dependents, all financial obligations discharged, and demonstrated acceptance of Kosovo's constitutional and legal order. Article 10.3 separately allows the President to naturalize a foreigner outside these standard criteria altogether, for 'special economic, social, cultural, sporting, scientific, political or professional interest' -- a discretionary exceptional-merit route distinct from the assessed standard track.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 years of legal residence, demonstrate language ability, financial self-sufficiency, and acceptance of the constitutional order, then apply.

evidence_required.document: Proof of sufficient means and discharged financial obligations

sources.title: Official Gazette of the Republic of Kosovo (government-hosted primary legal text) -- Law No. 03/L-034 on Citizenship, Article 10 (standard naturalization) and Article 10.3 (presidential exceptional-merit naturalization)
OCNAL (press) -- Kosovo's April 2026 citizenship-law reform: diaspora reacquisition cut from 9 documents/6 months/a fee to 1 document/30 days/free

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Kosovo). STATUS: DRAFT -- the standard naturalization mechanics are sourced to Law 03/L-034 (2008), tier 1, but that law has since been replaced twice, most recently by Law No. 10/L-023 (effective 6 May 2026), so this file is deliberately downgraded pending confirmation the 5-year/language/means thresholds survived unchanged. MAJOR, CURRENT, PROMINENTLY-FLAGGED EVENT: Kosovo's Interior Minister enacted a citizenship-law reform in 2026 that dramatically simplified DIASPORA REACQUISITION -- from up to 9 documents down to a single request plus a no-criminal-record declaration, from 6 months down to 30 days, and made it free -- framed by the government as fulfilling an electoral promise to strengthen ties with the diaspora. This same reform wave is tied to a genuinely CONTROVERSIAL, actively-disputed political dimension: separate but related amendments (citizenship and property law) specifically ease acquisition of status and property rights for ethnic Albanians from the Presevo Valley municipalities in southern Serbia (Presevo, Medvedja, Bujanovac) who migrated to Kosovo after 1999 -- Kosovo Serb community representatives and some Serbian-community political figures have publicly characterized this as a demographically-motivated move against Kosovo's Serb population, and critics argue it sits in tension with the EU-brokered Brussels Agreement normalizing Belgrade-Pristina relations. This dataset presents this as a live, disputed political controversy, not a settled fact in either direction. dual_citizenship_allowed set to true per Article 3 of the 2008 law, with the same supersession caveat noted throughout this country's citizenship files.
